steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Pilgrimage is not a sacrament and is not required by Christianity, but many Christians find it deepens their faith. Key reasons for pilgrimage include: seeking spiritual renewal, asking for healing, expressing devotion, walking in Jesus' footsteps, and connecting with Christian history.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: When comparing Lourdes and Iona, focus on the contrast: Lourdes is Catholic, associated with Mary and healing miracles, and attracts millions seeking physical cures. Iona is ecumenical, associated with contemplation, peace and social justice, and attracts those seeking spiritual renewal. Both are journeys of faith but with very different emphases.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Pilgrimage
steps.body: 1. For Pilgrimage questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Pilgrimage to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.body: Explain why Lourdes is an important place of pilgrimage for Catholics. | "Pilgrimage is a waste of time and money." Evaluate this statement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
